stem.en: No sooner had we sat down to eat ___ the fire alarm went off.

why.en: 'No sooner' is always paired with 'than': No sooner had we sat down than …
why.uz: «No sooner» doimo «than» bilan keladi: «No sooner had we sat down than …».
why.ru: «No sooner» всегда употребляется в паре с «than»: «No sooner had we sat down than …».

stem.en: It's high time the council ___ something about the potholes on this road.

why.en: 'It's high time' is followed by a past form with present meaning: the council did something.
why.uz: «It's high time» dan keyin hozirgi maʼnoda oʻtgan zamon shakli keladi: the council did something.
why.ru: После «It's high time» используется прошедшая форма со значением настоящего: the council did something.

stem.en: I'd rather you ___ my phone without asking me first.

why.en: 'Would rather' + another subject takes a past form for a present wish: I'd rather you didn't use …
why.uz: «Would rather» dan keyin boshqa ega kelsa, hozirgi istak oʻtgan zamon shakli bilan beriladi: «I'd rather you didn't use …».
why.ru: Если после «would rather» идёт другое подлежащее, для желания в настоящем нужна прошедшая форма: «I'd rather you didn't use …».

stem.en: ___ hard they tried, the volunteers could not clear the road before dark.

why.en: 'However + adjective/adverb' means 'no matter how': However hard they tried, …
why.uz: «However + sifat/ravish» «no matter how» maʼnosini beradi: «However hard they tried, …».
why.ru: «However + прилагательное/наречие» значит «как бы ни»: «However hard they tried, …».

stem.en: ___ for the quick response of the lifeguard, the swimmer might have drowned.

why.en: 'Had it not been for …' is an inverted third conditional meaning 'If it hadn't been for …'.
why.uz: «Had it not been for …» — inversiyali uchinchi shart gap, maʼnosi «If it hadn't been for …».
why.ru: «Had it not been for …» — инвертированное условное третьего типа: «If it hadn't been for …».

stem.en: The committee published a report ___ it set out its main recommendations.

why.en: In a formal relative clause the preposition can come before 'which': a report in which it set out …
why.uz: Rasmiy nisbiy gapda predlog «which» dan oldin kelishi mumkin: «a report in which it set out …».
why.ru: В официальном определительном придаточном предлог может стоять перед «which»: «a report in which it set out …».

stem.en: By the end of this year, my grandfather ___ at the same factory for forty years.

why.en: 'By' + a future point with a length of time takes the future perfect continuous: will have been working for forty years.
why.uz: «By» + kelajakdagi payt va davomiylik bilan future perfect continuous ishlatiladi: will have been working for forty years.
why.ru: С «by» + момент в будущем и длительностью нужен future perfect continuous: will have been working for forty years.

stem.en: He talks about the city as if he ___ there for years, but he only arrived last week.

why.en: 'As if' + past perfect describes something untrue about the past: he had not really lived there for years.
why.uz: «As if» + past perfect oʻtmish haqidagi haqiqatga toʻgʻri kelmaydigan holatni bildiradi: u yerda yillab yashamagan.
why.ru: «As if» + past perfect описывает то, что не соответствует действительности в прошлом: он там годами не жил.

stem.en:
Sardor rarely speaks in meetings, but when he does, people tend to stop what they are doing and listen.
What does the sentence suggest about Sardor?

options.en: He talks too much in meetings.
People usually ignore what he says.

why.en: People stop and listen when he speaks, which shows they value what he says.
why.uz: U gapirganda odamlar ishini toʻxtatib tinglaydi — demak, uning fikrini qadrlashadi.
why.ru: Когда он говорит, все откладывают дела и слушают — значит, его мнение ценят.

stem.en:
Although the recipe claims to take thirty minutes, anyone attempting it for the first time should allow at least twice as long.
What is the writer's point?

options.en: A first attempt will take an hour or more.
The recipe takes exactly thirty minutes.
Only experienced cooks should try the recipe.
Experienced cooks need at least an hour.

why.en: 'At least twice as long' as thirty minutes means an hour or more for a first attempt.
why.uz: Oʻttiz daqiqadan «at least twice as long» — birinchi urinishda kamida bir soat degani.
why.ru: «At least twice as long», чем тридцать минут, — это час или больше при первой попытке.

stem.en:
The village's only shop closed last spring; since then, older residents have relied on neighbours with cars to fetch their groceries.
What has happened since the shop closed?

options.en: Older residents depend on others to get their shopping.
Older residents now travel to the next town by bus.
A supermarket in town now delivers to older residents.
Some neighbours now sell groceries from their own homes.

why.en: Since the closure, older residents 'have relied on neighbours with cars to fetch their groceries'; no buses, deliveries or home shops are mentioned.
why.uz: Doʻkon yopilgandan beri keksa aholi oziq-ovqat olib kelish uchun mashinasi bor qoʻshnilarga tayanadi; avtobus, yetkazib berish yoki uydagi doʻkon haqida gap yoʻq.
why.ru: После закрытия магазина пожилые жители зависят от соседей с машинами, которые привозят им продукты; об автобусах, доставке или торговле на дому не сказано.

stem.en:
Critics dismissed the novel when it first appeared, and only decades later did it come to be regarded as a classic.
What happened to the novel?

options.en: Its reputation grew long after it was first published.
It lost most of its early popularity over the decades.
Critics praised it at first, but readers ignored it.
It was hailed as a classic soon after it appeared.

why.en: Critics first 'dismissed' it, and only 'decades later' was it seen as a classic: its reputation grew late, not early, and it never lost favour.
why.uz: Tanqidchilar avval uni rad etgan, faqat oʻn yillar oʻtib u klassika deb tan olingan: obroʻsi erta emas, kech oshgan.
why.ru: Сначала критики роман отвергли, и лишь через десятилетия его признали классикой: репутация выросла поздно, а не сразу.
